title: Bring the research station back online
audience: Learners approaching A-level physics, with optional GCSE bridges; curious adult explorers welcome
level: Introduction bridging GCSE to A-level DC circuits
outcomes: Explain closed-path charge flow and distinguish current from charge
Interpret potential difference as energy per unit charge
Predict how resistance changes current in ideal DC circuits
Apply conservation of charge and energy to series and parallel networks
Use current and potential-difference measurements to test a hypothesis
Relate power and energy to a station component budget
Diagnose unfamiliar faults and justify a repair using independent evidence
prerequisites: Multiply, divide and rearrange a one-step relationship
Read decimal quantities and SI unit prefixes; bridging help provided
scope: Ten short investigations of ideal DC resistors, source and switches, conservation, measurement, power, open faults and repair; optional unrestricted exploration within the bounded model
excluded: Resistivity, internal resistance and potential dividers are left to the existing deeper electricity-dc course
curriculum: AQA 7408 electricity informed, not exam-board branded or full specification coverage
sources: Existing electricity-dc module objectives and circuit-sim reference implementation
playConcept: A storm has isolated a research station. Restore useful equipment by constructing, measuring, predicting and diagnosing its real circuit states. More than one investigation order; experiments expose conservation.
decisions: Owner delegated subject/design choices; ten episodes selected
Ship ideal bounded resistor model and label its limits
assumptions: 5 to 12 minutes per core episode is an estimate
Basic ratios can be bridged without locking entry
